newsitem.title: CHINA: China refinery set to list 108 million A shares.
newsitem.headline: China refinery set to list 108 million A shares.

text.p: Chinese oil refiner Shijiazhuang Petrochemical Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would list 108 million domestic currency A shares on the Shenzhen bourse on July 31.

The company had raised net proceeds of 688.8 million yuan from an initial public offering of 120 million A shares, priced at 5.89 yuan each, earlier this month, the firm said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Of the 120 million A shares, 12 million were issued to the company's staff, it said, adding these shares would not be floated until six months after the listing of the 108 million shares.
The company, based in the northern province of Hebei, had an annual crude oil refining capacity of 3.5 million tonnes, the firm has said in a recent share issue prospectus.
Most of the crude oil, which accounted for 78 percent of the firm's production costs, was supplied by China National Petrochemical Corp, the prospectus said.
It said the company would invest all proceeds in a 3.57 billion yuan petrochemical joint venture, the construction of which began in 1996 for completion in 1999.
The project was financed by a 1.9 billion yuan loan from an Italian bank at an annual interest rate of 6.95 percent, it said.
The company forecast net profits of 209 million yuan for 1997, compared with 245 million yuan in 1996 and 297 million in 1995 under Chinese accounting standards, the listing statement said.
It did not explain the projected earnings slide.
Sales for 1997 were targeted at 3.38 billion yuan against 2.92 billion last year and 2.95 billion in 1995, it said.
Diesel accounted for 41.7 percent of its sales in 1996, with gasoline accounting for 40.5 percent, the prospectus said.
The company had 720 million outstanding shares, consisting of 600 million state shares, 12 million shares held by staff and 108 million A shares, according to the statement.
